teams.heading: Jake White names three uncapped players in Fiji's first squad for Japan
teams.body: New Fiji head coach Jake White has named his first Test squad, 28 players for the Centennial Test against Japan, and three of them are uncapped: Apolosi Vuniyawa, Kavekini Boselawa and Nacani Boginisoko. White has picked 16 forwards and 12 backs, without some European-based players. Fiji look to gain a measure of revenge on Eddie Jones' side after losing to them in last month's Pacific Nations Cup final, and the Test starts their preparations for November's matches against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: Hard selection news from Fiji's own camp, and it is new today, unlike the Nawaqanitawase story already run this edition.

teams.heading: Andy Goode calls England's failure to talk to Shaun Edwards 'mind boggling'
teams.body: Former England fly-half Andy Goode says no meaningful talks were held with Shaun Edwards, who has instead taken a coaching role with Argentina, and calls the omission 'mind boggling'. England, who have lost five of eight matches this year and conceded 29 tries, need England head coach Steve Borthwick to give attack coach Lee Blackett full licence, Goode argues. "It's mind boggling why you wouldn't at least have the conversation," he says, and he believes the RFU has blundered.

lead.why: It is England's own coaching decision, and it is a different story from the eligibility row already led today.

teams.heading: James A Lucas warns France's success could crush rugby like cricket
teams.body: Kick Off columnist James A Lucas argues France's success is itself the threat to rugby, dismissing the idea that the French are villains and saying their intentions are irrelevant. Lucas recalls a social-media plea asking the rugby gods not to let France kill the sport as India killed cricket, which drew puzzled, offended responses from France and its defenders. The sport would be poorer without France, those defenders countered, pointing to the number of players France employs and its profitable league.

lead.why: It is a new item about France's standing in the game, and it avoids the already-reported Flament injury and the women's series.

teams.heading: Leinster and Munster lead four Irish provinces into Champions Cup this weekend
teams.body: The four Irish provinces open their Champions Cup campaigns this weekend, the competition's first October start since 2018, after only three league games. Leinster, beaten 41-19 by Bordeaux-Bègles in May's final, have not won the trophy since 2018, while Munster dropped into the Challenge Cup last season after losing at home to Castres in their final pool game. Munster have not secured a home knockout tie in four seasons, and BBC Sport suggests springtime rugby at Thomond Park should be the aim.

lead.why: The only NEW item on the shortlist, and it covers all four Irish provinces starting their Champions Cup campaigns.

teams.heading: Italy concede 28.9 points a game across their last 11 matches
teams.body: Italy's defensive record over their last 11 matches is the figure that stands out. They conceded 318 points in that run, an average of 28.9 a game, and scored 190 in the same stretch. Their biggest win in the window was a 34-19 home victory over Chile in November 2025. Their next opponent is South Africa, so the conceding column is the one to watch.

teams.heading: Scotland's 33-17 win over Fiji was their latest result, in July
teams.body: Scotland's latest result was a 33-17 win over Fiji in July, in the Nations Championship group stage. Their last five games have brought three wins and two defeats, read most recent first as W L W L W. Their log record shows three games played, two won and one lost, with 108 points scored and 97 conceded. Their next game is against New Zealand in Round 4.

teams.heading: Wales trio Wainwright, Cracknell and Reffell start all Leicester's league games
teams.body: Wainwright, Cracknell and Reffell have started all three of Leicester's league games, a combination that had never played together before. Wins over Newcastle and Gloucester and a narrow defeat to Saracens have come with Wainwright and Reffell on the flanks and Cracknell at number eight. Wainwright, with 70 Wales caps, set up winger Gabriel Hamer-Webb for a try against Saracens on his debut. Tandy names his autumn squad next week, and this back row is making its case.

lead.why: The freshest Wales item in the pack, and it names three internationals in a settled Leicester back row that Tandy will be watching.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards' Pumas deal rules out role under Steve Borthwick
teams.body: Shaun Edwards' move to Argentina closes off any return to Steve Borthwick's England set-up, with Ruck reporting that he will not coach England at the 2027 World Cup. BBC Sport reported on 9 October that the former France defence coach has signed a deal with the Pumas running until the end of the 2027 World Cup in Australia. He and former Argentina hooker Mario Ledesma, who takes charge of the forwards, start work at the end of October, before November's Nations Championship matches against Ireland, Italy and France.

lead.why: The Edwards storyline is the only open Argentina thread in today's pack, and its England angle has now closed.

teams.heading: Sir John Kirwan calls Wallabies' bench a 'big problem' before second Bledisloe
teams.body: Sir John Kirwan, speaking on the Rugby Rivals podcast, believes the Wallabies have a "big problem" on their bench before Saturday's second Bledisloe Test in Sydney. His view is that the All Blacks' replacements lifted the level after the sides were level at 14-14 at the break in Auckland, while Australia's depth looked short in a 50-19 defeat. Kirwan doubted whether the squad has enough depth, and the Wallabies named a vastly inexperienced eight among their replacements last week.

lead.why: It is the strongest genuinely new item in the pack, and it turns the Wallabies' fly-half crisis into a question about squad depth.

teams.heading: Japan face Wales again after 24-23 loss in November 2025
teams.body: Japan meet Wales in Round four of the Nations Championship, their first match since the 15-42 loss to France. Wales beat Japan 24-23 in their previous meeting, in November 2025. In the log's three matches, Japan have won one, lost two and scored 62 while conceding 88. They sit 10th of 12 in the table.

teams.heading: Richie Mo'unga may miss November tests after calf injury, Rennie says
teams.body: Richie Mo'unga is progressing well from a calf injury, but Dave Rennie has conceded the fly-half may miss the opening games of the November tour. Rennie told reporters the injury is potentially a six-to-eight-weeker, and Mo'unga has been brought over so the team's medics can control his rehab. Damian McKenzie starts at 10 in Sydney on Saturday, and Rennie says the group still has three fly-halves for the Scotland, Wales and England games.

lead.why: A new injury to a key All Blacks fly-half, with a possible impact on the November tour, is the story fans will talk about, and it has not been reported in earlier editions.

teams.heading: Eben Etzebeth joins Sharks in week two; five Springboks miss EPCR opener
teams.body: Eben Etzebeth, the Springboks lock, is due to rejoin the Sharks' three-week European tour next week, having initially been missed off the 28-man list with a lower-limb issue. It seems the Sharks expect him to be fit sooner rather than later. Five other Springbok Test players, Ox Nche, Thomas du Toit, Andre Esterhuizen, Ethan Hooker and Edwill van der Merwe, are left at home for the EPCR Challenge Cup opener against Lou in France.

lead.why: It is the freshest hard news on Springbok availability in the pack, and the Rennie high-ball story has already run today.
